  "relation": "REFINED",
  "consensus_summary": "Primary meaning across responses is God's final eschatological judgment through Christ: evaluation of all persons' deeds and relation to Christ, producing separation of righteous (eternal life) from wicked (condemnation), supported by creeds and key NT/OT texts (Matt 25, Rev 20, etc.). Common alternatives include temporal/historical judgments on nations, realized/present judgment in response to Christ, purifying discipline of believers, vindication/deliverance of the oppressed, human moral discernment/church discipline, and minority views (dual bema/white-throne judgments, preterism, annihilationism/universalism).",
  "book_summary": "Judgment is the law's ruling and the ruler's office: what God declares due, kept like a commandment and owed first to the widow, fatherless, stranger, and poor. To judge is to rule and deliver by the law (judges were saviors; a king to judge us and fight our battles); the righteous pray for judgment and creation rejoices at its coming; condemnation is one verdict of the office, not the office itself.",
  "consensus_core_identification": "God's (especially final eschatological) evaluation of persons/deeds resulting in a just verdict of separation, vindication, or condemnation",
  "book_core_identification": "the ruler's office of declaring and enforcing by law what is due (especially protective justice and deliverance for the vulnerable)",
  "core_relation": "COMPATIBLE_OVERLAP",
  "extension_relation": "PARTIAL_RECLASSIFICATION",
  "boundary_disagreement": "Consensus primary centers final universal evaluation and dual destinies (including condemnation as definitional); book centers the ongoing office of just rule/deliverance for the weak and treats condemnation as merely one non-definitional verdict, elevating prayer for judgment and creational rejoicing.",
  "material_contradiction": "None; book reorients priority and essence without denying evaluation, verdicts, or eschatological coming of judgment.",
  "rationale": "Minimum cores both concern divine justice involving ruling and verdicts, so the general referent (judgment as God's just action) is preserved and not replaced. Book materially refines precision and boundaries by defining the office itself (ruling/delivering what is due, first to the vulnerable) as the core and explicitly demoting condemnation from definitional status; this reclassifies cases the consensus primary treats as central while elevating vindication/deliverance (already present as a common alternative). Not MATCH (different priority and precision), not DIVERGENT (no replaced referent or exclusive contradiction), not NOVEL (vindication/office/deliverance senses appear in alternatives).",
  "citation_support": "STRONG",
  "strongest_objection": "Creedal and dominant NT usage (Matt 25, Rev 20, 2 Cor 5, John 5, etc.) make final evaluation and separation the settled primary sense; the book's office-of-deliverance framing risks under-weighting universal accountability and punitive verdicts.",
  "confidence": "high"
}
